summary.title: Building a Facial Recognition Pipeline with Deep Learning in Tensorflow
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a facial recognition pipeline that aligns faces with Dlib, generates 128-dimensional FaceNet-style embeddings with Inception ResNet V1 in TensorFlow, and classifies identities with an SVM, all run inside Docker.
keywords: how to do facial recognition in python
takeaways: Detect the largest face in each image with Dlib and align it using the inner eyes and bottom lip landmarks.
Generate 128-dimensional face embeddings with a pre-trained Inception ResNet V1 (FaceNet-style) model in TensorFlow, using transfer learning.
Train a scikit-learn SVM on the embeddings to classify identities; the author reports about 90.8% accuracy at 25 epochs on LFW.
Use Docker to package TensorFlow, OpenCV and Dlib so the hard-to-install dependencies run consistently.
summary.summary: The tutorial walks through a facial recognition pipeline on the LFW dataset. It covers the background of FaceNet and triplet loss, then preprocesses images with Dlib (largest-face detection, landmark-based alignment and cropping) run in a Docker container with parallel processing. Next it loads images through TensorFlow queues, creates 128-dimensional embeddings from pre-trained Inception ResNet V1 weights, and trains a scikit-learn SVM on them. The author reports about 85.0% accuracy after 5 epochs and 90.8% after 25 epochs, and links the full code on GitHub.
